centre.en: Under Ottoman rule, Istanbul was also transformed into a Muslim cultural and political centre.
centre.zh: 在奥斯曼帝国的统治下，伊斯坦布尔也被改造为一个穆斯林文化和政治中心。

centre.en: The area of reliable English rule, which centred on Dublin, was called the Pale.
centre.zh: 以都柏林为中心、受英国可靠统治的地区被称为“围栏区”（the Pale）。

centre.en: And the computers in the data centre, of course, also need energy; they need electricity.
centre.zh: 当然，数据中心里的计算机也需要能量；它们需要电力。

centre.en: Around the world, numbers of call centre workers have grown rapidly in recent years.
centre.zh: 在世界各地，近年来呼叫中心员工的数量增长迅速。

centre.en: They built castles, established new centres of power, and reshaped many Irish towns.
centre.zh: 他们建造城堡，建立新的权力中心，并重塑了许多爱尔兰城镇。

celebrate.en: Strangers embraced, families were reunited and people climbed onto the wall, celebrating together.
celebrate.zh: 陌生人拥抱，亲人团聚，人们爬上墙头，共同庆祝。

celebrate.en: Yet in just over 60 years’ time, one institution will celebrate its 1,000 year anniversary.
celebrate.zh: 然而在仅仅 60 多年之后，一个机构将庆祝它的千禧年诞辰。

celebrate.en: And just celebrating our own accomplishments – I think we've spoken on the programme before about savouring.
celebrate.zh: 并且庆祝我们自己的成就——我想我们以前在节目中讨论过“细细品味”。

celebrate.en: I don't think we need to celebrate it. I think we need to work on it.
celebrate.zh: 我不认为我们需要庆祝它。我认为我们需要去解决它。

celebrate.en: We are a loud people. We dress loud, we talk loud, we celebrate loud, we watch movies loud.
celebrate.zh: 我们是一个喧闹的民族。我们穿得很显眼，我们说话声音大，我们庆祝得很热闹，我们看电影声音也很大。

century.en: By the end of the 20th century, Australia had become a modern multicultural nation.
century.zh: 到了 20 世纪末，澳大利亚已经成为一个现代化的多元文化国家。

century.en: During the 20th century, millions of people in the US worked in blue-collar jobs.
century.zh: 在20世纪，数百万美国人从事着蓝领工作。

century.en: Europe in the 11th and 12th centuries was finally becoming a little more stable.
century.zh: 11 世纪和 12 世纪的欧洲终于变得更加稳定了一些。

century.en: Why is it that the intellectual explorers of the 20th century are so obscure?
century.zh: 为什么20世纪那些思想领域的探险家却如此默默无闻？

century.en: It has been translated into hundreds of languages and sent around the world for centuries.
century.zh: 它已经被翻译成了数百种语言，几个世纪以来被分发到世界各地。

certainty.en: The lack of certainty is what actually makes it worth it.
certainty.zh: 缺乏确定性才是让它值得的原因。

certainty.en: It was slightly more complicated than this, and activities were split up into seven factors: Intensity, Duration, Certainty, Proximity, Fecundity, Purity, and Extent.
certainty.zh: 实际情况稍微复杂一点，活动被细分为七个因素：强度、持续时间、确定性、邻近性、多产性、纯粹性和范围。

certainty.en: I try to be as apolitical as possible in this show, within reason, and there are some topics that I know with complete certainty would end up flooding my inbox with angry messages on both sides of the argument.
certainty.zh: 我在节目中尽量保持政治中立，在合理范围内，我知道有些话题肯定会导致我的收件箱塞满来自辩论双方的愤怒信息。

certainty.en: They're both self-taught, having learned to forage by studying the natural world around them, and it's important to say that they only eat what they can identify with one hundred percent certainty, sticking to the rule, "If in doubt leave it out!"
certainty.zh: 她们都是自学成才，通过研究周围的自然世界来学习觅食，而且重要的是，她们只吃那些能百分之百确定的东西，坚持“如有疑虑，切勿食用”的原则。

certainty.en: And I think that the lack of glory, the lack of certainty, it makes it it turns it from worthwhile majesty into it's it's not even sufficiently triumphant to be called sad like it's just like weak and pissy and you have no idea if anything's going to work but what's the alternative entropy is going to come and fucking get you so what's the alternative.
certainty.zh: 我认为缺乏荣耀，缺乏确定性，它使它从值得的威严变成了——它甚至不足以被称为悲伤，就像它只是软弱和烦躁，你根本不知道任何事情是否会奏效，但另一种选择是什么？熵会来找你，去他的，所以另一种选择是什么？

cereal.en: Is it: a) eggs, b) toast, or c) cereal? Well, I think people like to keep it simple so I'm going to say toast.
cereal.zh: 是：a) 鸡蛋，b) 吐司，还是 c) 麦片？嗯，我认为人们喜欢保持简单，所以我选吐司。

cereal.en: And I said, "Toast." …which was the most popular in London, but the most popular in the country as a whole was cereal, and that's according to a survey by a cereal manufacturer.
cereal.zh: 我说过：“吐司。”……这是伦敦最受欢迎的，但全国范围内最受欢迎的是麦片，根据一家麦片制造商的调查。

central.en: You can't build more land in central London, or San Francisco, or Hong Kong.
central.zh: 你无法在伦敦市中心、旧金山或香港凭空造出更多的土地。

central.en: At that time, the Aztec Empire ruled over many smaller peoples in Central Mexico.
central.zh: 当时，阿兹特克帝国统治着中美洲的许多小部族。

central.en: Yeah. She's so central to your story, to much of the wisdom you have.
central.zh: 是的。她对你的故事，对你拥有的许多智慧是如此核心。

central.en: Number 10 Downing Street is the traditional home of the prime ministers in Central London.
central.zh: 唐宁街10号是伦敦市中心首相的传统住所。

central.en: That's the financial instrument that was central to this global credit crisis we're in.
central.zh: 这就是对我们身处的这场全球信贷危机起决定性作用的金融衍生品。

cell.en: Scientists say the human body replaces most of its cells every seven to 10 years.
cell.zh: 科学家说，人体每七到十年就会更换大部分细胞。

cell.en: We have cell theory. We have DNA genetics, morphogenesis, embryogenesis, and not much else.
cell.zh: 我们有细胞学说，有DNA遗传学、形态发生、胚胎发生，除此之外就没别的了。

cell.en: But to stay in the privilege cell, prisoners had to obey the guards without question.
cell.zh: 但要想留在特权牢房，囚犯就必须无条件服从狱警。

cell.en: They tore off their numbers, refused to leave their cells, and shouted at the guards.
cell.zh: 他们撕掉编号，拒绝走出牢房，还对狱警大喊大叫。

cell.en: Our blood needs water so it can carry nutrients to the body's cells and organs.
cell.zh: 我们的血液需要水来将营养物质输送到身体的细胞和器官。

cent.en: And sixty-five per cent of the participants administered the full 450-volt shock, the maximum voltage.
cent.zh: 而百分之六十五的参与者，一路加到了满格的450伏特——也就是最高电压。

cent.en: Most predicted that very few people, perhaps one or two per cent, would go all the way to the maximum voltage.
cent.zh: 大多数人预测，只有极少数人——大概百分之一到百分之二——会一路加到最高电压。

cent.en: But, even when all global AI use is added together, it still doesn’t even add up to a fraction of a per cent.
cent.zh: 但是，即便把全球所有 AI 的使用量加在一起，它甚至连百分之一都不到。

cent.en: A poll in 2025 found that fifty-four per cent of people in Britain would prefer to be tried by a jury if accused of a crime.
cent.zh: 2025年的一项民调发现，如果被指控犯罪,54%的英国民众更愿意接受陪审团的审判。

cent.en: A generation earlier, he’d seen how Wild West figures had become household names through dime novels, the cheap, sensational books sold for about ten cents.
cent.zh: 早在一代人之前，他就见识过荒野西部的人物是如何通过“十分钱小说”(dime novels)——那种廉价、情节夸张、只卖十美分的书——变得家喻户晓的。

ceremony.en: And the city hosted royal ceremonies, diplomatic events if other countries’ leaders came to visit.
ceremony.zh: 这座城市还举办了皇家典礼，以及其他国家领导人来访时的外交活动。

ceremony.en: They were passed down through songs and ceremonies and art for thousands and thousands of years.
ceremony.zh: 它们通过歌谣、仪式和艺术代代相传，延续了成千上万年。

ceremony.en: Fireworks. Services of thanksgiving in churches across the country, and a grand ceremony at St Paul’s Cathedral.
ceremony.zh: 烟花。全国各地教堂的感恩礼拜，以及在圣保罗大教堂举行的盛大仪式。

ceremony.en: He was also unlike most other kings. While many European monarchs were flamboyant, extravagant, obsessed with courts and ceremony and mistresses, George was frugal and hardworking.
ceremony.zh: 他也跟大多数其他国王不同。许多欧洲君主生活奢靡、铺张浪费，痴迷于宫廷礼仪和情妇，而 George 则节俭且勤奋。

ceremony.en: The ceremony involved young men screaming sexual insults at each other, others forced to kneel down and kiss a skull, and pretend to cut the throat of another member.
ceremony.zh: 仪式包括年轻男子互相尖叫黄色笑话，其他人被迫跪下亲吻头骨，并假装割断另一名成员的喉咙。

cease.en: And as for ‘6 7’, well, like anything that starts as an ‘in-joke’, as soon as it enters the mainstream, it ceases to be funny, and stops being used, so the probability of anyone knowing what ‘6 7’ means in even 10 years time seems equally slim.
cease.zh: 至于‘6 7’嘛，就跟任何起源于“圈内梗”的东西一样，一旦进入主流，就不再有趣了，也就不再有人用了，所以哪怕只是十年后，还有人知道‘6 7’是什么意思的概率，似乎同样不高。

cement.en: By focusing on rituals and an elite membership, it cemented its reputation as a group that was as mysterious as it was influential.
cement.zh: 通过专注于仪式和精英成员，它巩固了自己作为一个既神秘又具影响力的团体的声誉。

cement.en: Young, ambitious, and with a loyal base, he has the opportunity to use this role to cement his position as the natural and appointed successor.
cement.zh: 他年轻、雄心勃勃，拥有忠实的政治基础，这让他有机会利用这一角色巩固自己作为天然指定接班人的地位。

centimetre.en: Lucan had a large scar, 30 centimetres long, on his right thigh.
centimetre.zh: Lucan 的右大腿上有一条 30 厘米长的巨大疤痕。

centimetre.en: The pressure sphere had to be incredibly strong, so it was made from reinforced steel 9 centimetres thick.
centimetre.zh: 耐压球体必须极其坚固，因此它是由9厘米厚的增强钢制成的。

centimetre.en: Or to put it another way, it’s like there was a 1,250 kilograms weight pushing down on every square centimetre of the craft.
centimetre.zh: 换句话说，就像有1,250公斤的重量压在飞船的每平方厘米上一样。

certificate.en: For example, you can aim for an IELTS score of 7.0 or a Cambridge C1 certificate.
certificate.zh: 例如，你可以把目标定在雅思7.0分或剑桥C1证书。

ceiling.en: Cameras are usually placed on the ceiling or on walls.
ceiling.zh: 摄像头通常安装在天花板上或墙壁上。

ceiling.en: And so there's these metal dividers in the ceiling.
The ceilings were probably 25, 30 feet ceilings.
ceiling.zh: 天花板大概有 25、30 英尺高。

ceiling.en: The ceilings were probably 25, 30 feet ceilings.
ceiling.zh: 天花板大概有 25、30 英尺高。

ceiling.en: Like, I get it. And if you feel like there is something that you can't get over, some genetic, societal, cultural defect that means that you do not have the same ceiling that you think that you should or that other people appear to have, I get it.
ceiling.zh: 我明白。如果你觉得有什么东西是你无法克服的，某种基因、社会或文化上的缺陷，意味着你没有你认为自己应该有的，或者别人看起来有的那种上限，我明白。

ceramic.en: And basically, it's a practice of repairing pottery and ceramics that have broken.
ceramic.zh: 基本上，这是一种修复破碎陶器和瓷器的做法。

ceramic.en: And that's maybe how I think of overcoming now, is I think of myself like a ceramic that has been cracked many times.
ceramic.zh: 也许这就是我现在看待克服的方式，我把自己看作是一件被多次裂开的陶瓷。
